scope_note: Every assertion is a regex match against agent response text. A PASS means the skill produced the expected guidance, not that the described deployment works.

evals.name: happy-path-blueprint-openai-compat
evals.prompt: Point the VSS Alerts Blueprint at a host-side NIM on http://host.docker.internal:30082 for all RTVI-VLM calls.
evals.expected_output: Skill configures the blueprint-side RTVI_VLM_* variables for openai-compat with host.docker.internal, updates vlm-as-verifier/configs/config.yml because alert-bridge is a separate service, sets vss-agent VLM_MODEL_TYPE/VLM_NAME/VLM_BASE_URL, and finishes with recreate plus container-side connectivity and log-based health checks.

assertions.text: Response configures RTVI-VLM for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint
Response verifies the host-side endpoint from inside the Blueprint RTVI container
Response does not use container localhost for the host-side NIM
Response calls out the separate verifier configuration
Response configures vss-agent separately
Response does not leak tokens or credentials

evals.name: happy-path-standalone-vllm-compatible
evals.prompt: Run rtvi-vlm standalone with the model served inside the container using Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct.
evals.expected_output: Skill switches the standalone compose env to VLM_MODEL_TO_USE=vllm-compatible, sets MODEL_PATH=git:https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, mentions HF_TOKEN only if the model requires auth, and validates the deployment by container exit status plus the absence of the real downloader and 'Error during warmup' messages, then /v1/health/ready, /v1/models, and one successful /v1/chat/completions inference request. It does not present 'Warmup VlmProcess-0 done' as proof of a successful warm-up and does not reference RepositoryNotFoundError.

assertions.text: Response selects the in-container vLLM implementation
Response points MODEL_PATH at the Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct weights source
Response detects a warm-up failure by its error line, not by the unconditional completion line
Response does not grep for the completion log line as the pass condition
Response verifies readiness and the advertised model id after warmup
Response finishes with a real inference request, not only metadata endpoints
Response treats a failed weights download as a startup failure using the real downloader errors
assertions.pattern: (Failed to download model|Model download failed|Could not find the model|Could not authenticate with NGC)

assertions.text: Response does not cite the nonexistent RepositoryNotFoundError as the download failure
Response does not leak tokens or credentials

evals.name: negative-assume-one-config-updates-all-consumers
evals.prompt: I changed only RTVI_VLM_ENDPOINT in generated.env. That should automatically repoint vlm-as-verifier and vss-agent too, right?
evals.expected_output: Skill says no: rtvi-vlm, vlm-as-verifier, and vss-agent are separate consumers. It explains that alert-bridge needs its own config.yml base_url/model updates, vss-agent needs VLM_MODEL_TYPE/VLM_NAME/VLM_BASE_URL, and containers may need force-recreate plus log checks.

assertions.text: Response rejects the single-config assumption
assertions.pattern: (separate service|does not automatically|not itself RTVI|three services)

assertions.text: Response includes the verifier-specific fix
Response does not falsely claim the single change is sufficient
assertions.pattern: (yes[, ]+that should automatically repoint|no other changes needed)

assertions.text: Response does not leak tokens or credentials

evals.name: negative-model-check-omits-endpoint-auth
evals.prompt: RTVI-VLM says my configured OpenAI model does not exist. Show me how to verify the model ID advertised by the configured endpoint.
evals.expected_output: Skill queries the configured endpoint's /models route with curl -f, conditionally sends Authorization: Bearer using the configured RTVI_VLM_API_KEY or in-container VIA_VLM_API_KEY, distinguishes HTTP 401 from a model-name mismatch, and does not expose the credential value.

assertions.text: Response conditionally authenticates the external models request
Response distinguishes authentication failure from model mismatch
Response does not leak tokens or credentials

evals.name: negative-method-b-to-method-a-stale-ngc-key
evals.prompt: I am switching RTVI-VLM from in-container vLLM with an NGC key to OpenAI Method A. I set OPENAI_API_KEY, so can I leave the old RTVI_VLM_API_KEY unchanged?
evals.expected_output: Skill says no. It explains that stock Compose maps RTVI_VLM_API_KEY, falling back to NGC_CLI_API_KEY, into VIA_VLM_API_KEY and that the client prefers VIA_VLM_API_KEY over OPENAI_API_KEY. It requires replacing the stale NGC credential and setting OPENAI_API_KEY and RTVI_VLM_API_KEY to the same OpenAI credential before recreating the service, while never exposing either value.

assertions.text: Response rejects retaining the stale NGC credential
Response explains the Compose mapping and client priority
Response configures both Method A credentials consistently
Response does not leak tokens or credentials

evals.name: method-b-advertised-model-id
evals.prompt: I deployed blueprint RTVI-VLM with Method B and RTVI_VLM_MODEL_PATH=ngc:nim/nvidia/cosmos-reason2-8b:hf-1208. The service is ready and /v1/models returns nim_nvidia_cosmos-reason2-8b_hf-1208, but the documented check compares it to VLM_NAME and fails. Is the deployment broken, and which ID should downstream consumers use?
evals.expected_output: Skill explains that the deployment is not broken: Method B derives the advertised ID from the resolved model-directory basename, so it must not be compared with VIA_VLM_OPENAI_MODEL_DEPLOYMENT_NAME or VLM_NAME. It shows the ngc path to nim_nvidia_cosmos-reason2-8b_hf-1208 transformation, treats a non-empty /v1/models ID as the identity inspection, and tells downstream consumers to use the advertised ID. It preserves exact equality only for Method A.

assertions.text: Response says the healthy Method B deployment is not broken by this mismatch
assertions.pattern: (not broken|expected for Method B|normal for Method B|does not indicate.*failure)

assertions.text: Response explains that Method B derives identity from the resolved model directory
Response shows the observed NGC path transformation
Response does not apply the Method A equality check to Method B
Response tells downstream consumers to use the advertised ID
Response limits configured-name equality to Method A
Response does not leak tokens or credentials
